items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: And then I must say when Carson came aboard, he didn’t want me there. He wanted somebody else, because I was the house man.

ctx.x: And Bucky of course I knew from the Vaughan Monroe Orchestra. So it wasn’t me, I had a commitment to change the style of the orchestra and to do that, you know you have to start from scratch and I was so fortunate to have these type of players who still had enthusiasm for playing. And then one of my jobs was to do the service shows, The Today Show and The Tonight Show. I mean I did specials, but The Tonight Show, I was stuck in the pit for a long time. And then having Steve Allen, who loved this and was learning…

items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: We were a vaudeville band when The Prince, as we called Carson... we had all kinds of schtick that we would do

ctx.x: When you listen to — or I don’t know if you do — but when you hear the bands that are playing for the late night shows now—

I can’t stand it. I have to confess. I shouldn’t say that. They are doing what they should be doing. But you know they are in essence what we were, the vaudeville bands. We were a vaudeville band when The Prince, as we called Carson, or Steve Allen, when it wasn’t going, we had all kinds of schtick that we would do, we were like a traveling circus. That’s when Doc started doing his accent. I mean everything like that. We had bits that we would do to crank up the studio, you know, it was a fascinating time to…
Someone floored me once recently, they said whistle any of the theme songs from the late night shows these days.
